top_story.headline: PAC Tells FEC a Federal Court Ordered Its Former Treasurer to Repay $29,413.77
top_story.dek: Forward Together PAC answered an FEC inquiry on Tuesday about restitution it lists as a debt owed to the committee.
paragraphs: Forward Together PAC of Williamsburg, Virginia filed a Form 99 on October 6 responding to a September 1 Request for Additional Information on its July 2026 Quarterly Report. The FEC's letter flagged a Schedule D debt described as "Court-ordered restitution payment owed to the Committee," and said it appeared to be related to an unauthorized use of committee funds.

In the response, the committee says a federal court has ordered its former treasurer, Katherine Buchanan, to pay restitution totaling $29,413.77, which it therefore reports as money owed to the committee. It cites FEC advisory opinions 1991-38 (DeConcini) and 2005-04 (Boehner) and says it explained the matter in an earlier Form 99 filed July 20, 2026 and has made other filings giving context.

The filing does not say how much was taken, over what period, or how much has been repaid; the committee says only that it "continues to work with the Commission on its resolution." Separately, two other committees drew FEC questions this week over transactions the agency labeled apparent unauthorized disbursements: James Osyf for Congress ($2,058.01) and Friends of Chris Bennett ($112.67), both listed under Requests for Additional Information below.

sections.headline: Four Sitting Members Draw RFAIs, Two Over Joint-Fundraising Disclosure; Three Others File Form 99 Replies
paragraphs: Seven sitting members of Congress appear in this window: 9 FEC letters went to the committees of Delegate James Moylan, Delegate Kimberlyn King-Hinds, Sen. Katie Britt and Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, and Rep. Mary Miller, Rep. Jennifer Kiggans and Rep. Adam Gray filed Form 99 responses. The Moylan and King-Hinds letters (seven of them) share a theme: transfers from American Battleground Fund that the FEC says weren't disclosed through a joint fundraising representative designation.

items: Sen. Katie Britt (R-AL), committee Britt for Alabama INC — RFAI on the July 2026 Quarterly Report: Schedule A lists one or more contributions that appear to exceed the contribution limits (the specific donors are in an attachment to the FEC letter) (received 10/06). Filing.

Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL-8), committee Friends of Raja for Congress — RFAI on the April 2026 Quarterly Report: Schedule D shows apparent credits against debt owed to Spiros Consulting, and the FEC asks for clarification of those credits (received 10/05). Filing.

Delegate James Moylan (R-GU), committee James Moylan for Congress — RFAI on the July 2026 Quarterly Report: transfers from American Battleground Fund look like joint-fundraising proceeds, but that committee isn't listed as a joint fundraising representative on the Statement of Organization, and the transfers appear on the wrong summary line (should be Line 12) (received 10/06). Filing.

Delegate James Moylan (R-GU), committee James Moylan for Congress — RFAI on the April 2026 Quarterly Report: same issue — transfers from American Battleground Fund look like joint-fundraising proceeds but the committee isn't disclosed as a joint fundraising representative, and they are on the wrong summary line (received 10/06). Filing.

Delegate James Moylan (R-GU), committee James Moylan for Congress — RFAI on the 2025 Year-End Report: the combined 2025 reports show joint-fundraising transfers from American Battleground Fund without the required memo Schedule A itemizing the committee's share of gross contributions (received 10/06). Filing.

Delegate Kimberlyn King-Hinds (R-MP), committee King-Hinds for Congress — RFAI on the October 2025 Quarterly Report: transfers from American Battleground Fund appear to be joint-fundraising proceeds, but it is not disclosed as a joint fundraising representative; the report also puts some activity (including offsets to operating expenditures) on the wrong summary line (received 10/06). Filing.

Delegate Kimberlyn King-Hinds (R-MP), committee King-Hinds for Congress — RFAI on the July 2026 Quarterly Report: memo entries on Schedule A were counted in totals, which deflates reported cash on hand, and transfers from American Battleground Fund aren't backed by a joint fundraising representative designation (received 10/06). Filing.

Delegate Kimberlyn King-Hinds (R-MP), committee King-Hinds for Congress — RFAI on the 2025 Year-End Report: no memo Schedule A itemizing the committee's share of joint-fundraising gross receipts from American Battleground Fund, and that committee isn't listed as a joint fundraising representative (received 10/06). Filing.

Delegate Kimberlyn King-Hinds (R-MP), committee King-Hinds for Congress — RFAI on the April 2025 Quarterly Report: cycle-to-date (Column B) totals on Lines 7(a), 7(c), 17 and 22 look wrong, and the beginning cash balance doesn't match the ending balance of the 2024 Year-End Report (received 10/06). Filing.

Rep. Mary Miller (R-IL-15), committee Mary Miller for Congress — Form 99 responds to a Sept. 3 RFAI on its July Quarterly Report about three debts to Launchpad Strategies ($9,262.03, $9,130.84 and $9,646.48, totaling $28,039.35) that disappeared from the report: says the invoices were billed to the candidate committee by mistake, belonged to a joint fundraising committee and were rebilled (received 10/06). Filing.

Rep. Jennifer Kiggans (R-VA-2), committee Kiggans for Congress — Form 99 responds to a Sept. 3 RFAI on apparent excessive contributions: says any contribution lacking donor reattribution or redesignation was refunded within 60 days (received 10/05). Filing.

Rep. Adam Gray (D-CA-13), committee Adam Gray for Congress — Form 99 responds to an Aug. 30 RFAI on Column B totals on its July Quarterly Report: says it amended the report to correct them; signed by treasurer Lauren Decot Lee, who also signed the Villegas for Congress letter and is listed as treasurer on the Juliana for Illinois RFAI (received 10/05). Filing.

sections.headline: 35 RFAIs to Challengers, Open-Seat Candidates, PACs and Parties
paragraphs: Most of these are routine disclosure fixes: general-election money held by candidates who are out of the race, missing 48-hour notices, wrong summary totals and payroll allocation questions. Two items stand out for apparent unauthorized use of committee funds (James Osyf for Congress and Friends of Chris Bennett), and four committees got "Verification of Form 1" letters, including one registered under a sexually explicit name referring to Rep. Lauren Boebert. The FEC's keyword scan flagged four of those letters for "fraud," but the word appears only in the standard penalty language about false statements.

sections.headline: 38 Form 99 Submissions From Challengers, PACs and Parties
paragraphs: Most are replies to RFAIs, plus a handful of loan-forgiveness statements, no-activity statements and termination requests. Residual cash on hand after a campaign ends is the recurring subject: four campaigns told the FEC they are keeping money without committing to personal use.

items: America Is the Way PAC — asks to terminate its registration as a voluntary filer; says it registered Sept. 3, 2026, received and spent nothing, and is ceasing operations (treasurer Zachary J. Kuck) (received 10/06). Filing.

Aswar — a handwritten, scanned FEC Form 3 filed on paper under a Form 99 listing; the scan is largely illegible (summary pages show near-zero activity), so figures could not be confirmed (received 10/06). Filing.

Ben Samuels for Congress — responds to a Sept. 2 RFAI about residual cash on hand: says funds support aligned candidates and causes and none has been converted to personal use (received 10/04). Filing.

Build the Barn PAC — responds to an Aug. 31 RFAI about contributors who gave to Wahls for Iowa for the general election: confirms all were refunded within 60 days and further refunds will appear on its October Quarterly Report (received 10/04). Filing.

California Republican Party Federal Acct. — California Republican Party responds to an RFAI on its June Monthly Report: says "Digital Media Consulting-less than 25% FEA" payments were administrative website, analytics and design work that did not refer to a candidate, and explains salary allocation between Line 30(b) and Schedule H4 (received 10/05). Filing.

California Republican Party Federal Acct. — responds to an RFAI on its July Monthly Report with the same explanation of "Digital Media Consulting-less than 25% FEA" payments and salary allocation (received 10/05). Filing.

California Republican Party Federal Acct. — responds to an RFAI on its amended March Monthly Report: says it corrected the Schedule H4 administrative category to match Schedule H1, so period totals are correct and no further amendment is needed (received 10/05). Filing.

California Republican Party Federal Acct. — responds to an RFAI on its amended February Monthly Report: says it amended Schedule H4 to match the Schedule H1 ratio, did not over-transfer from its non-federal account, and repeats the "Digital Media Consulting" explanation (received 10/05). Filing.

Campaign for Democracy PAC — responds to a Sept. 1 RFAI on its July Quarterly Report, arguing every travel and subsistence reimbursement was fully itemized with memo entries, so no amendment is needed (treasurer Analea Patterson) (received 10/06). Filing.
Chuck Uribe for California Congressional District 4 — states only that "there was no activity during this time period" (received 10/06). Filing.

Coloradans for Kerry Donovan — responds to a Sept. 2 RFAI: says it will keep residual cash for a possible future federal run by Kerry Donovan, with no office or cycle chosen, and won't use funds for personal use (received 10/05). Filing.
Congressional Black Caucus PAC — Form 99 with no readable text beyond the committee header (received 10/05). Filing.

Deliver Energize Succeed PAC — FEC notice dated Oct. 5 to treasurer Jen Slater that the committee failed to file its Form 1M (multicandidate status notification) electronically as required for committees above $50,000 or voluntarily filing electronically (received 10/05). Filing.

Dem Turnout Fund — responds to a Sept. 1 RFAI about how it collects missing employer and occupation information for donors: describes a 30-day follow-up note to donors and a donor-database record of the follow-ups as its "best efforts" process (received 10/05). Filing.
Felicia Harris Hoss for Congress — Form 99 with no readable text beyond the committee header (substance likely in an attachment) (received 10/06). Filing.

Forward Together PAC — responds to a Sept. 1 RFAI about a "Court-ordered restitution payment owed to the Committee" on Schedule D, saying a federal court ordered former treasurer Katherine Buchanan to pay $29,413.77 in restitution, which it reports as a debt owed to the committee. See today's Top Story (received 10/06). Filing.

Frese for Congress — says it has not raised or spent more than $5,000 through Sept. 30, 2026 and so isn't required to file the October Quarterly Report; candidate Jeffrey Frese, California's 10th District (received 10/05). Filing.

Jami Floyd for Congress — responds to an Aug. 31 RFAI on its April Quarterly Report: amended to replace the vague purpose "Political Consulting" and to add memo entries itemizing a reimbursement to Sandor Weiss (received 10/05). Filing.

Johnson Leadership Fund — responds to an Aug. 31 RFAI on its July Quarterly Report: says a contribution from Yum Brands Inc Good Government Fund was reported accurately (given 2/12/26, deposited 5/7/26) and that event expenses were catering, site rental and travel; treasurer Lisa Lisker (received 10/05). Filing.

Lone Star Liberty PAC — responds to an RFAI: says it filed an independent-expenditure report for a runoff as a 48-hour report when it should have been a 24-hour report, making the filing one day late, and says staff have reviewed the rules (received 10/05). Filing.
Lorenzo Rios for Congress — responds to an Aug. 30 RFAI on general-election contributions: says all were timely refunded, to be reflected on the October Quarterly Report (received 10/05). Filing.

Los Angeles County Democratic Central Committee — responds to an Aug. 31 RFAI on Schedule H1: says its April–June 2026 monthly reports disclose the fixed administrative percentage and note that payroll was for employees spending 25% or less of their time on federal election activity (received 10/06). Filing.
Lucio for Congress — candidate Daniel Lucio forgives all remaining personal loans and advances owed to him by the committee (Loan Forgiveness; amount not stated) (received 10/06). Filing.
Mark Smith for Congress — candidate Mark Smith says he forgave all personal loans he made to his campaign, totaling $378,259.26 (treasurer Steve Martin) (received 10/05). Filing.

Massachusetts Democratic State Committee - Fed Fund — responds to a Sept. 1 RFAI on its July Monthly Report: says a contribution from International Union of Painters and Allied Trades Political Action Together was not from its federal account and has been refunded (to be reported Oct. 20), while one from IBEW Local 103 Federal Political Action Committee was federal (received 10/05). Filing.

Massachusetts Republican Party — responds to an Aug. 31 RFAI on its July Monthly Report, saying administrative expenses were properly disclosed and salary and wages were allocated on Schedule H4 because no employee spent more than 25% of their time on federal election activity (received 10/05). Filing.
Massachusetts Republican Party — second Massachusetts Republican Party Form 99 with no readable text beyond the header (received 10/05). Filing.

Mike Johnston for US Senate — responds to a Sept. 2 RFAI about significant residual cash on hand: says it is aware of the restrictions on using the funds, has complied, and is "weighing our options" (received 10/06). Filing.

Montana Republican State Central Committee — responds to an Aug. 31 RFAI on its July Monthly Report: says utilities are included in its office rental and that a payment to Ultra Graphics described as donation envelopes will be amended to "MTGOP Printing: letterhead, and letterhead envelopes" (received 10/05). Filing.

New Era Leadership — responds to an RFAI on its amended June Monthly Report: says a $25,000 debt to AL Media LLC for a supplemental ad buy was incurred June 1, not May 29, and admits a separate 24-hour independent-expenditure report for that $25,000 buy should have been filed by June 2 but was overlooked; the earlier buy was $125,000 (received 10/05). Filing.

Ola Victory Fund — responds to a Sept. 2 RFAI on its 2025 Year-End Report: says a $24,000 contribution on Dec. 31, 2025 was the personal money of federal candidate Ola Nesheswat Hawatmeh, sent through the wrong fundraising link and allocated entirely to People For Ola, so it was not excessive; asks that this resolve the issue and allow the pending termination review to finish (received 10/06). Filing.

Richoz for Congress — Form 99 whose readable page is a U.S. House Committee on Ethics late-fee waiver form for financial disclosure statements and periodic transaction reports; no explanatory text was legible (received 10/05). Filing.

States Win — responds to an RFAI on its July Quarterly Report: corrected a contribution from Vote Save America from $5,000 to $10,000 and added a previously omitted $5,000 disbursement to its non-federal account States Win, Inc.; treasurer Cassie Tinsmon (received 10/05). Filing.
Theresa Greenfield for Iowa — responds about residual funds on its April and July 2026 reports: says they'll be used per FEC rules and not for personal use (received 10/05). Filing.
Timmins for Congress — candidate Patrick Timmins files a statement of loan forgiveness with the committee's Termination Report (amount not stated in the legible text) (received 10/05). Filing.

Villegas for Congress — responds to an Aug. 30 RFAI on its July Quarterly Report: corrects a received date on a contribution from Immigrants' List and says a contribution first reported from "Haystaq DNA" was reattributed to Ken Strasma because it is a single-member LLC; treasurer Lauren Decot Lee (received 10/05). Filing.

Vote Courage 4 Democracy Fund — a very small independent-expenditure-only committee formed in August 2026 explains late filings: it filed a paper Form 3X Aug. 14 and will refile electronically, filed a 48-hour report late for $13,470 and $10,000 in expenditures, and refunded $23,870 in contributions that were first attributed to Ansercall LLC and later to donor George Jordan; asks for leniency (received 10/05). Filing.
You Can Push Back — Form 99 submitted with no readable text beyond the committee header (the substance appears to be in an attachment not captured in the text layer) (received 10/06). Filing.

footer.coverage_window: Filings received by the FEC October 4–7, 2026 (Pacific), excluding filings reported in prior editions.
footer.sources: FEC filings API (F99 and FRQ); FEC Schedule A/B itemized transactions; FEC candidate and committee records.
